basics.name: Dhruv Tomar
basics.label: Undergraduate Student
basics.summary: An undergraduate student passionate about computing in biology.

work.name: Van Doren Lab of Migration Biology, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
work.summary: Investigating the effects of light pollution on bird flight behavior using 3D object tracking in thermal videography.
highlights: Optimized background subtraction methods for thermal video object tracking.
Trained and optimized a YOLOv8 machine learning model to improve object detection performance.
Performing extrinsic calibration of thermal cameras and analyzing over 10,000 tracks using MATLAB and Python (NumPy, pandas, SciPy, TensorFlow).

work.name: Engineers for Exploration, University of California San Diego
work.summary: Summer 2025 NSF-funded Intern in the Engineers for Exploration program.
highlights: Collaborated with National Geographic explorers on two large-scale bioacoustic data mining projects, characterizing soundscapes with little to no labeled data.
Applied template matching and unsupervised deep learning to build a Graph Neural Network pipeline uncovering latent links between audio features and environmental variables.

Pioneered a modular Python package enabling scalable, cross-dataset bioacoustic analysis and integration into future ecological research workflows using libraries such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, and Librosa.

work.name: Grainger College of Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
work.summary: Teaching an mentoring a section of ~20 Computer Science students in a first-year engineering orientation course (ENG 100) on academic, career, and campus life topics.
highlights: Facilitating student learning and community-building using curated lesson materials.
Attending weekly instructional meetings to review pedagogy and curriculum design.

work.name: Illini Wildlife and Conservation Club
work.summary: Organize monthly general meetings and speaker events, inviting speakers to discuss topics in wildlife and conservation biology.
highlights: Participate in philanthropy such as turning off lights around campus to conserve energy and picking up litter around campus.

volunteer.summary: Survey 20+ buildings on campus during the bird migration season several times a week for bird-window collisions following survey protocols and log them via ArcGIS QuickCapture.
highlights: Collect specimens for use in teaching and research.

awards.title: James Scholar Honors Program
awards.summary: The James Scholar Honors Program is a selective academic program at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign that recognizes outstanding undergraduate students for their academic excellence and leadership potential.

publications.name: Studying Domain Shifts in Bioacoustic Recording Style With Information Theory (Preprint)
publications.summary: A major challenge in machine learning (ML) for studying passive acoustic monitoring is the domain shift between directional, handheld, well-labeled focal audio data and omnidirectional, passively recorded, under-labeled soundscapes. ML models trained on the vastly more labeled focal recording datasets struggle to generalize when tested on soundscape recordings. Research in this area has typically focused on the methodology behind training ML models, both to study and alleviate the domain shift. However, less work has been done in quantifying the domain shift hypothesis beyond model performance and species density. This potentially limits our understanding of the factors behind domain shift. We find that the Ecoacoustic Global Complexity Index (EGCI), an acoustic complexity index rooted in information theory, can effectively describe the domain shift and assist in productive research of this domain shift. We demonstrate EGCI's effectiveness in three experiments. First, we show that an SVM can easily classify between soundscape and focal recordings using only EGCI values, with an average accuracy of 81.08% (minimum approx 65%). Second, we demonstrate that EGCI, in conjunction with species density via linear regression, can predict soundscape performance and reveal that EGCI values are negatively correlated with soundscape loss. Finally, we demonstrate that data augmentation, shown in the literature to alleviate domain shift in model performance experiments, reduces the KL-divergence between the EGCI distributions of focal recordings and soundscape recordings.
